s: Snowflake-style unique ID issuance: time-ordered, coordination-free, sortable identifiers at massive scale.
w: 64-bit layout: timestamp-ms | machine-id | sequence-counter. Each node generates independently - no central bottleneck; IDs sort chronologically enabling range scans/index locality. Machine-ids assigned statically or via coordinator; sequence resets per-ms allowing thousands per ms per node. Clock-rewind guarded by spin-wait logic.
use: Primary keys for sharded databases (range-friendly vs random UUIDs)
avoid: Security-sensitive exposure (sequential ids leak volume/timing - hash or encrypt if needed)
pits: NTP step-backwards duplicates - monotonic guards or accept brief pauses
tips: vs UUIDv4: randomness kills B-tree locality; vs UUIDv7: same idea standardized - mention both
